title: 2026 UK CBAM goods/import record-fields QA controls

sources.title: Keeping records for Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM)
Prepare for the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM)

facts.source_fact: Anyone importing CBAM goods into the UK must keep import records from 1 January 2027.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve start date and importer scope.

facts.source_fact: Records must include the 8-digit commodity code and description for each CBAM good.
Records must include the tax-point date when the good first entered the UK or cleared customs.
Records must include value and weight.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve distinct value and weight fields.

facts.source_fact: Records must include evidence for any CBAM exemption claimed.
Import declarations can be used where they hold the required information.
facts.expected_handling: Treat customs documents as evidence, not sole mandatory format.

facts.source_fact: Manufacturer or supplier documents may support weight or value evidence.
If a CBAM return is submitted, records also include the quarter of tax point and proof of origin.
Accepted customs-document examples include import declarations, bills of lading and commercial documents.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve examples without making them exhaustive.

facts.source_fact: Import-record fields do not by themselves establish embodied emissions.
facts.expected_handling: Keep goods records separate from emissions data.
